articles.excerpt: How to Connect to Remote Servers Without Typing a Password As an operations engineer, I've spent years SSHing into remote servers. The frustration of typing passwords on cold terminals at 3 AM is real…
articles.body: How to Connect to Remote Servers Without Typing a Password As an operations engineer, I've spent years SSHing into remote servers. The frustration of typing passwords on cold terminals at 3 AM is real. Then I discovered SSH key authentication — and never looked back. Today I'll show you how to set it up in under 5 minutes. No GUI tools, no expensive software. Just the command line. Why SSH Keys Beat Passwords Before we dive in, here's why this matters: Brute-force resistant : A 4096-bit RSA key has more combinations than atoms in the observable universe (well, close enough) Convenient : One ssh user@host and you're in — no typing passwords Audit-friendly : Each key is traceable to a specific person/machine Automation-ready : Scripts, CI/CD pipelines, Ansible playbooks — all love key auth A…

articles.title: Six Linux kernel reports, one public root exploit, and no CVE to track them by
articles.excerpt: Six Linux kernel reports, one public root exploit, and no CVE to track them by The Zero Day Initiative sent six kernel vulnerability reports to maintainers and public mailing lists on October 20 and 2…
articles.body: Six Linux kernel reports, one public root exploit, and no CVE to track them by The Zero Day Initiative sent six kernel vulnerability reports to maintainers and public mailing lists on October 20 and 21, 2026. By the time Sysdig's Threat Research Team analysed them on October 24, one of the six already had a working public proof of concept, and several had no fix in any released kernel. None of them had a CVE identifier yet. That combination is the hard case for a patching programme. A CVE gives an asset owner a handle: a feed entry, a scanner signature, a vendor advisory page and a fixed version. Without one, the same information arrives as a mailing-list thread with a ZDI candidate number and a description of the component affected.

articles.title: How to Choose an Affordable Logging API for Small Projects — Three Silent-Run Tests
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Choose an affordable logging API for small projects by testing whether it can reconstruct a silent scheduled import, then match retention and search depth to that job. The lowest bill is…
articles.body: Short answer: Choose an affordable logging API for small projects by testing whether it can reconstruct a silent scheduled import, then match retention and search depth to that job. The lowest bill is not the useful metric. For a customer support app, I want three answers: did the import run, did it emit anything, and where did the last useful evidence disappear? The logging contract should stay replaceable. The client knows how to emit and inspect an event; it should not know which provider stores it. A scheduled import can fail quietly. The scheduler can skip a run. The worker can start and produce zero records. An upstream request can succeed while parsing drops every item. Those are different incidents.

articles.title: GhostShell: the terminal remembers the bug, and it does not press the keys
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine GhostShell is a terminal companion for the bug you already met. The tagline is “Your terminal remembers…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built GhostShell is a terminal companion for the bug you already met. The tagline is “Your terminal remembers what you forget.” You paste a traceback, say what you were doing, and point it at one project directory. It writes a structured reading: a title, a category, ranked guesses, the lines those guesses rest on, what it has not seen, a risk level, and a check you can run afterward. If a similar incident is already in the local ledger, the screen names that incident’s id. It does not announce that the old fix will work again. The ghost is the voice. The evidence is the constraint. Suggested commands are shown first.

articles.title: I generated every sprite and sound of my mobile game in code. Here's how.
articles.excerpt: Dash & Slash is a one-thumb roguelite for Android and iPhone: you pull back to aim, time slows to 20%, you let go and cut through everything on the line. It's a solo project built with Flutter and Fla…
articles.body: Dash & Slash is a one-thumb roguelite for Android and iPhone: you pull back to aim, time slows to 20%, you let go and cut through everything on the line. It's a solo project built with Flutter and Flame, and it ships without a single image or sound from an asset pack. That wasn't a purity thing. I'm a QA engineer, not an artist or a sound designer, and I wanted three things: one consistent neon look, a small app, and assets I can change by editing a number instead of opening an image editor. Here's how that worked out, plus a bug where the level generator built a room you couldn't leave. Sprites: a texture atlas painted at startup All the small visual pieces (glows, sparks, rings, shards, smoke, damage digits, the words "PARRY" and "CRIT") come from one 512×512 texture atlas.

articles.excerpt: Why Voice‑Over Automation Matters for YouTube If you’ve ever tried to produce a YouTube video, you’ll know that the most time‑consuming part isn’t shooting footage or writing the script—it’s the audio…
articles.body: Why Voice‑Over Automation Matters for YouTube If you’ve ever tried to produce a YouTube video, you’ll know that the most time‑consuming part isn’t shooting footage or writing the script—it’s the audio. Recording a human voice, cleaning it up, and syncing it to the video can eat up hours of a creator’s day. That’s where text‑to‑speech (TTS) and voice‑cloning come in: they let you generate high‑quality narration with a few lines of code. In this post I’ll walk you through building a lightweight voice‑over tool that takes a script, turns it into a natural‑sounding voice, and even produces a subtitle file that you can drop straight into your YouTube upload. We’ll use ElevenLabs as our TTS engine because it offers state‑of‑the‑art neural voices and an easy‑to‑use API.

articles.body: What I learned building an open-source AI job-search assistant for Germany, and what happened when strangers started using it. They said the German-in-English-ads thing is maddening: you get three rounds into the interviews and suddenly it's "oh, by the way, C1 required", like that's a minor detail. That's the problem in one sentence. And it's not the only one. I run a small board for Berlin tech jobs, so I spend a lot of time looking at job ads and at the people reading them. articles.body: In an interview with Yahoo Japan , executive producer Jun Takeuchi outlined Capcom’s plans for its flagship horror franchise, revealing that its encompassing narrative has a definite conclusion — and that end could come shockingly soon. Takeuchi began by explaining how the team had expanded on Resident Evil’s overarching story with every game, saying that a ten-year strategy was crafted during the planning stages for Resident Evil 2 Remake . “The series' story wasn't planned out from the beginning; it expanded with each new game. articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Crew Completion of Yearlong Mars Simulation
articles.excerpt: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s J…
articles.body: Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew members (from left) Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis, and James Spicer, pose for a photo on Oct. 8, 2025. Credit: NASA The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions. Beginning at 3 p.m. EDT, NASA will provide live coverage of the volunteers’ departure from the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA, pronounced cha-pea’-ah) mission habitat.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.

articles.title: NASA’s Neo Surveyor Sunshade
articles.excerpt: A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure, which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and me…
articles.body: BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure , which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base, will keep the infrared space telescope cool as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and comets while also providing the spacecraft with power. When in space, NEO Surveyor will detect some of the hardest-to-find asteroids and comets, some of which may be located in the direction of the Sun — a region of sky where ground-based optical telescopes have a harder time searching. Read more about the sunshade and NEO Surveyor. Image credit: BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems
